source.title: [MODEL] Lane: the availability record — bitemporal, append-only, our clock (addendum 252)
source.body:
## The lane

`availability-record` (docs/roadmap.json) is a bitemporal, append-only store of what was knowable about who plays, stamped by our clock. It generalises the cups' Step B store (`schema.CupLineupObservation`). The board places it **immediately below the model lanes** (252 item 7): "the NHL and NFL-QB lanes cannot declare without it — it is the first tooling that unblocks a model lane rather than waits beside one".

It is tooling, not a model. It prices nothing, it is no Desk input, and it writes no row to any existing table (item 5).

## Steps (item 7; no existing date moves)

| # | Step | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The schema PR: item 1, the migration, the query command `availability`, tests 6(a)-(c), (g), (h). Filed with this Issue. | code | 2026-11-10 |
| 2 | The nflverse depth-charts feed (3(a)), its chain `availability-daily` and its 08:45 UTC timer. | code | 2026-11-12 |
| 3 | The paid feed's adapter specified, if the operator names one on 11-13 (3(c)). | architect | 2026-11-14 |
| 4 | The NHL landing feed (3(b)) and its watch, the `availability-observe` timer. | code | 2026-11-17 |
| 5 | The graph projection's candidate comparison (item 4). | code | 2026-11-20 |
| 6 | The paid feed's adapter, if one is named (3(c)). | code | 2026-11-21 |
| 7 | The graph projection's rebuild, `availability-graph-rebuild` (item 4). | code | 2026-11-25 |

The bulletins lane (addendum 250, #826) queues behind the schema and nflverse PRs and ahead of the projection. The first host reads and the timers' enablement are the architect's blocks. Thursday's migration tag does not carry any of it.

## The ruling, in full (ARCHITECT 2026-11-04 13:05 ET, addendum 252)

> ARCHITECT 2026-11-04 13:05 ET — addendum 252: THE AVAILABILITY RECORD (lane availability-record, new): a bitemporal, append-only store of what was knowable about who plays, stamped by our clock, generalised from the cups' Step B store; two free feeds first (nflverse depth charts, the NHL landing read); a graph projection as step 2, never a record. The operator's direction of 11-04 12:38 ET ("let's go") on my proposal of 12:35.
>
> 0. WHY. Every supplier in the operator's sourcing report (11-04) sells current state or post-hoc history; none preserves what it said before a game. The NHL lane (#105) and the NFL QB term (#427) both stalled on exactly that absence. The fix is ownership: observe early, stamp with our clock, never overwrite — the discipline Step B already lives under (schema.CupLineupObservation: one row per fixture, kickoff and poll; append-only; explicit failed, partial, empty and missed rows; the first complete observation preserved and every later answer its own row). This lane makes that the general store for availability facts in every sport. A season from now we hold a pregame record no vendor sells, and a model term can be built "only from what was readable at or before the cut-off", the cups' rule, in the NHL and the NFL too.
>
> 1. THE MODEL, bitemporal and append-only. Two tables, both created by one migration, both written by ingest commands only, both read mode=ro by everything else:
>    (a) `availability_observations` — one row per fetch: sport; source (a fixed vocabulary, item 3); endpoint (the URL or file name, no secrets); the match_id where the fetch is per game (NULL for a league-wide file), the stored kickoff then; poll_label where polled on a schedule (the probe's T-120 … T-0); scheduled_at; fetched_at (OUR clock, UTC); http_status; payload_sha256; payload_path (the raw answer kept on disk under logs/availability/<source>/<date>/, never under data/, never mirrored); status: complete | partial | empty | failed | missed (Step B's five, the same meanings); late; error (redacted); rows_asserted. NOTHING UPDATES OR DELETES A ROW. A fetch that raised is a row; a poll whose time passed with no call is a row.
>    (b) `availability_assertions` — one row per fact a payload asserted, keyed to its observation: observation_id; sport; kind (a fixed vocabulary: depth_rank | projected_starter | confirmed_starter | eventual_starter | inactive | injury_status | plays_for); player_id (ours, NULL with the source's id beside it when unmapped: source_player_id, player_name verbatim); team_id (ours; NULL + source_team verbatim when unmapped); match_id (NULL for a team-level fact); attrs JSON (pos_abb, pos_slot, pos_rank, status text, the side); source_stamp (THE SOURCE'S OWN TIME for the fact: nflverse's `dt`; NULL where the source gives none — the NHL landing gives none); recorded_at (= the observation's fetched_at, denormalised for the as-of query). No valid_to column and no update: an interval is DERIVED — a fact holds from its observation to the next observation of the same source that asserts the same (kind, player, team[, match]) differently, or that asserts the slot to someone else. "As of T" is one query: the newest observation per source with the chosen clock <= T, and its assertions. That is StackState's time travel in two tables and a WHERE clause.
>    THE TWO CLOCKS, ruled now so no term argues it later: `recorded_at` is OUR knowledge; `source_stamp` is the source's claim. A live-era record, a forward confirmation and a closing-time input use `recorded_at` only (what we had on our disk before the cut-off). A backfilled row (recorded_at later than source_stamp by more than the feed's cadence: nflverse's season file reaches back to its first load, so our first fetch records weeks of history at once) is usable ONLY in a backtest labelled "source-stamped" in its run record and its gate text, never in the live-era record; a term that wants it declares that in its bar. Both clocks are kept on every row so either reading can be audited.
>    Mapping (law 4): a player or team the source names that we cannot map stays NULL with the source's text beside it; mapping is by the existing tables' source ids (players.gsis_id / espn_id where we hold them, nhl player ids as nhl_goalies stores them) and never by name alone; an unmapped row is counted on the ingest's console and in a receipt, never dropped and never guessed.
>
> 2. THE QUERY SURFACE (read-only cli, one command): `availability --sport S --as-of INSTANT [--clock recorded|source] [--match-id N | --team T] [--kind K]` prints the facts in force at the instant under the chosen clock, each with both stamps and its observation; `--history` prints every assertion for the key in time order so a flip shows. The same function is the one a model term, the bulletin's teams section and the Cockpit will read; there is no second path.
>
> 3. THE FEEDS, in order. Each is its own ingest command, its own adapter, its own source vocabulary word, its own fixture tests on saved payloads, and lands as its own PR after the schema PR.
>    (a) nflverse DEPTH CHARTS (source `nflverse_depth_charts`): the release file for the season (github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data, release tag depth_charts, the 2025+ format: dt, team, player_name, espn_id, gsis_id, pos_grp_id, pos_grp, pos_id, pos_name, pos_abb, pos_slot, pos_rank — the dictionary as published; the 2023–2024 weekly files are a DIFFERENT shape and are NOT ingested by this feed: a second adapter later if a backtest wants them, labelled source-stamped). One fetch a day on the host after nflverse's ~07:00 UTC load (a new chain `availability-daily`, timer 08:45 UTC, inside no other chain; UNMETERED; failure receipted and paged as a sync-step failure, stopping nothing). Each fetch is one observation; its NEW rows (dt later than the newest source_stamp we hold for the source) become assertions of kind depth_rank (attrs: pos_grp, pos_abb, pos_slot, pos_rank), one per player-slot; the fetch's payload sha256 is kept, and a fetch whose file is byte-identical to the last is a `complete` observation with rows_asserted 0. Licence CC BY 4.0: the source word carries the attribution, and any output that uses the facts (a bulletin, a page) prints "Depth charts: nflverse (CC BY 4.0)". A QB1 from this feed is a DAILY RANK, not a game-day confirmation (the report's own limit): kind depth_rank says so; nothing here writes projected_starter.
>    (b) THE NHL LANDING READ (source `nhl_api_landing`): per game of the NHL day (the probe's schedule read: GET /v1/schedule/<date>, game types 2 and 3), the landing page at the probe's offsets (T-120, T-90, T-60, T-45, T-35, T-30, T-15, T-0) — each poll an observation with its poll_label — asserting projected_starter per side from matchup.goalieComparison.<side>Team.leaders[0] (playerId, name beside it) EXACTLY as scripts/nhl_leaders_order_receipt.py reads it, and the boxscore at T+20 asserting eventual_starter (the goalie with toi above zero; two in net = two rows, flagged; none = an `empty` observation) — post hoc, kind-labelled, never a pregame fact. The polls run under a watch on the host (an `availability-observe` timer every five minutes, the cup-observe pattern), each poll stamped by our clock; a poll more than five minutes past its time is a `missed` row. The receipt's reading of leaders[0]'s reliability STANDS as read on #105; this feed records what the page asserted and when, which is a fact whatever the page's reliability, and it is the free NHL pregame record from the day it runs.
>    (c) A PAID FEED, IF THE OPERATOR NAMES ONE ON 11-13 (SportsDataIO's Starting Goaltenders by Date is the report's candidate): the same table, source word `sportsdataio_goalies`, kind projected_starter with attrs.confirmed from the response's Confirmed field, polled on the same watch; its adapter is specified with the decision, not before. The 11-13 step's wording stands; what changes is the cost of "none": with (b) running, "none" leaves the NHL lane a free pregame record rather than nothing.
>    THE EVIDENCE RULING (the report's open question, answered): our own stamped observation of a source's response, fetched before the cut-off and kept unaltered (payload sha256, the raw file on disk), IS the pregame evidence. A supplier's assignment timestamp is welcome as source_stamp and never required.
>
> 4. STEP 2, THE GRAPH PROJECTION (after 3(a) and 3(b) are on the host): a nightly rebuild of the record into an EMBEDDED graph engine on the host — file-based, no server, Cypher — nodes Player, Team, Game, Observation; edges from the assertions carrying kind, recorded_at, source_stamp and the derived interval; rebuilt whole from SQLite (mode=ro) by one command, `availability-graph-rebuild`, as the last step of availability-daily; its file under logs/, never under data/, never backed up, never mirrored, deletable without loss. NEVER written by a chain other than its rebuild, NEVER read by the Desk, a prediction, an export or a gate; a failed rebuild is a receipt line and stops nothing. Code's first PR for this step is a one-page comparison of the embedded candidates — name, licence, maintenance state as of the PR's date (that field moved this year; the state is checked, not remembered), Python binding, Cypher dialect, file format — and I pick on it; nothing is installed before the pick. The projection is the lookup and exploration surface (the Cockpit, the bulletins' teams section, my own reads); any feature it suggests is a candidate term that goes through its gate like every other.
>
> 5. WHAT THE LANE NEVER DOES: no model change; no Desk input; no row written to lineups, match_participants, injuries or any existing table (the record is its own two tables; the existing stores are untouched); no provider call from a closing run (the record is read, never fetched, inside a closing); no backdating (a fact recorded after its game is post hoc and labelled so); no deletion ever; no payload under data/; no secret in an endpoint string; no scraping of a source whose terms forbid it (nflverse's licence is explicit; the NHL API is the one we already read; a paid feed's terms come with the decision).
>
> 6. TESTS (the acceptance set): (a) append-only — the ingest commands expose no update or delete path, and a test asserts the tables' row counts only grow across a replay of saved payloads; (b) the as-of query under each clock on a synthetic history with a flip, a backfilled row and a missed poll — the recorded clock never returns the backfilled row before its fetch; (c) the five statuses on saved payloads: complete, partial (a team unmapped), empty, failed (a raised call), missed (a scheduled poll with no call); (d) the nflverse adapter on a saved 2025-format file: every column read by name (law 1), the 2023–2024 shape refused with its reason; (e) the NHL adapter on the probe's saved payloads (the same files the leaders-order receipt reads): leaders[0] per side, two in net, no goalieComparison; (f) a payload with an unmapped player keeps its name and NULL id; (g) the derived interval on a sequence of observations equals the flip the history shows; (h) nothing under data/ after any test.
>
> 7. ORDER AND DATES (a new lane `availability-record` in docs/roadmap.json with these steps; no existing date moves; its Issue filed with the schema PR; the board places it immediately below the model lanes, since the NHL and NFL-QB lanes cannot declare without it — it is the first tooling that unblocks a model lane rather than waits beside one): the schema PR (item 1, the migration, the query command, tests 6(a)–(c), (g), (h)) opens in the next free slot after #825's merge-from-main push and the parity PR — due 11-10; the nflverse feed (3(a), its chain and timer) due 11-12, so the first host observations precede the 11-13 decision; the NHL landing feed (3(b), the watch) due 11-17; the paid adapter, if named, specified 11-14 and due 11-21; the projection's candidate comparison due 11-20, the rebuild due 11-25. The bulletins lane (addendum 250) queues behind the schema and nflverse PRs and ahead of the projection. Each PR body names its commands and arguments; no block ships to the operator; the first host reads and the timers' enablement are my blocks. Thursday's migration tag does not carry any of it.
